tools.name: compare_players
tools.description: Compare any two NFL players head to head for fantasy football: points per game in the requested scoring format, volume stats, bye weeks, and which one produced more. Use this for start/sit, draft, and trade questions about two specific players.

tools.name: get_rankings
tools.description: Fantasy football rankings for a position in a given scoring format, ordered by points per game. Positions: qb, rb, wr, te, flex, k, def. Use this for "who are the best X" and draft board questions.

tools.name: get_player
tools.description: A single player's fantasy profile: positional rank, points per game in all three scoring formats, season stats, games played, and bye week.

tools.name: search_players
tools.description: Find players by partial name, team abbreviation, or position. Use this when a name is ambiguous or only partly known before calling the other tools.

tools.name: get_positional_scarcity
tools.description: How steep the fantasy dropoff is at each position in a given scoring format, measured from the top player to replacement level. Use this for draft-strategy questions like whether to take a running back or a wide receiver first.

tools.name: get_bye_conflicts
tools.description: Given a list of players, report which bye weeks two or more of them share. Use this for roster planning and draft questions about stacking byes.

tools.name: get_weekly_matchup
tools.description: Who a player faces in a given week of the 2026 season, whether it is home or away, and how generous that opponent has been to that position. Use this for in-season start or sit questions that name a week, which the season-long tools cannot answer.

tools.name: get_adp_market_gaps
tools.description: Players whose consensus average draft position disagrees most with their actual production ranking. A player taken EARLIER than his production is being drafted on expectation (a rookie, a new situation, a bounce-back); one taken LATER is being drafted on doubt. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_players" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Find players by partial name, team abbreviation, or position. Use this when a name is ambiguous or only partly known before calling the other tools.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
